evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Not present. Rep opens with 'we have saw your that you have book move on the 11th of November' and immediately begins gathering logistics without any framing of the call's time commitment or promise of a dependable quote.
evidence_quotes.discovery_basics: Name (Sarah Copeland) confirmed at greeting. Move date (November 11, implicitly; October mentioned confusingly early). City-to-city route: both locations in San Antonio (4906 Worst Back Parkway to 14818 Mystic Main). Approximate size: 1,125 sq ft at origin, 2,086 sq ft at destination mentioned. All four technically touched but delivery is chaotic and not clean.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Never asked. Rep proceeds directly into logistics probing ('do we have any additional room') with no open-ended discovery of customer concerns or priorities.
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Property types (apartment, house) covered. Floor/stories (3rd floor, 2-story) covered. Rooms (2 bedrooms origin, 4 bedrooms destination) covered. Walking distance (10–15 feet to truck, ~20 seconds up stairs) covered. Special considerations (heavy items: TV, bookshelf, entertainment console; weight limit check) covered. Parking logistics (driveway steep, street parking) covered. Missing: no explicit ask about other potential obstacles or moves between origin rooms. Partial but substantial.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Rep gives '4 and a half to five hours, estimated cost would be $960' but provides no typical range for this size home, no personalization to customer's prep level or concerns, and no anchoring language. Partial at best.
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Trip fee / overnight fee not mentioned. Packing materials fee not mentioned. 'Not a guess' framing absent. 2.5-hour minimum not mentioned. 15-minute increments not mentioned. Only statement: 'we're timely based' and advice to pack small items to reduce time/cost. Partial.
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Not asked. Rep delivers estimate and immediately pivots to confirmation email logistics with no 'Does that feel fair?' and no pause for customer reaction.
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: No closing of loop on any promises or guarantees — none were delivered.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Not asked. Rep ends with 'feel free to let us know you can email, call us or text us at anytime' but never asks 'What's still concerning you about this move?' or equivalent.
evidence_quotes.catch_all_asked: Not asked. No 'Anything coming with you we haven't talked about?'
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Never asked. Rep never says 'Would you like our help with your move?' Booking is confirmed by customer saying 'Okay, thank you' in response to confirmation email mention, but there is no explicit ask for the business.
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: Move date (November 11, but opening was confused about October/November — ambiguity remains). Phone number not confirmed. Arrival window not confirmed. Crew size not confirmed. Addresses stated by rep but not explicitly confirmed by customer as correct. Notes for crew about customer concerns not documented. Partial — some details stated but not systematically confirmed.

top_strength: Rep gathered detailed logistics across two locations methodically (floor level, walking distance, special items, parking constraints, room count) and stayed focused on the practical details needed for the estimate.
coaching_note: This call skipped Section 1's framing entirely — no time-box or promise of a dependable quote — and never asked the customer about their concerns, priorities, or what they want answers to; add the 'Other than price, what are your biggest concerns?' question early and deliver the Two Promises (On-Time Guarantee and No Worries Damage Coverage) before closing, both completely missing here.
